Conversation reuse

Provider session reuse, cache affinity, final replay refusals, and explicit unsupported paths.

About 5 min read · 2 sections

On this page
01 Final refusals instead of hidden replay 02 Evidence and operations

Gateway preserves the caller's chat, instructions, selected model and account, permissions, and tool execution. It reuses native provider sessions where that transport supports them, and stable cache routing where the API requires full history. Sending history over HTTP is not evidence that the model processed the whole prefix again. Provider-reported cache reads establish reuse; missing counts remain unknown.

Transport Reuse and boundaries
Codex subscription Direct Responses HTTP, not one CLI per request. Caller cache keys, account-scoped encrypted reasoning and turn-state headers remain intact. When a client supplies a conversation ID but omits a cache key, Gateway derives a stable account/conversation key. Anonymous calls are not grouped. The subscription endpoint does not support previous_response_id.
Claude subscription Live sessions are the default. Matching histories append new items; complete tool results plus caller updates use acknowledged queued input. Explicit replay mode remains an opt-in compatibility choice. Warmup and explicit compaction/prewarm/memory requests can run standalone.
Copilot subscription Live sessions are the default. Complete pending results followed by caller messages use acknowledged session.send immediate admission before result delivery. A warm session is not evicted for a newcomer.
Chat Completions, including Qwen HTTP requests carry history. Opted-in local-router session affinity keeps a conversation on its worker. Equivalent catalogs and schema object keys are canonicalized to avoid accidental prefix changes. Actual KV/prefix reuse belongs to the inference server.
Anthropic API HTTP history with ephemeral cache breakpoints. Equivalent catalogs and schema objects use stable translated tool positions.
OpenRouter and OpenCode Existing explicit caller cache/session keys and documented provider affinity headers are preserved. Provider cache accounting remains authoritative.
Grok subscription Live sessions are the default: one grok agent stdio (ACP) process per conversation behind a mandatory tool-less agent profile, with caller tools as held calls on a loopback MCP endpoint. Matching histories (the pending tool outputs, or new user messages after a finished turn) continue it; every other history, and any request for a conversation whose session already ended (including the original request again, also after a gateway restart: the ended record is persisted), is a final 400 session_continuity_unavailable, never a replay. Requests without a conversation id, and compaction/prewarm/memory, run standalone (grok -p), which still refuses historical turns. No automatic model switch is made. See Grok sessions.

Final refusals instead of hidden replay

An ordinary live request that cannot attach because of capacity, concurrent work, startup failure or an unavailable adapter ends with HTTP 400 session_continuity_unavailable. A failed live CLI, queued-input admission or tool-result delivery also ends without an automatic one-shot retry. This applies after partial output or usage as well: Responses receives a final stream code so the client does not reconnect and silently reseed the failed request. Deterministic tool, confinement and malformed-stream failures retain their original diagnostic class and charged usage, but use final client errors across Responses, Messages and nonstreaming HTTP. Transient availability/throttle recovery keeps its existing behavior.

A Claude tool-name rejection deliberately closes its confined CLI without a crash hold. The failed response still ends without replay; only a later caller request may replace the process, through the existing cache budget. This applies to fixed unknown/unavailable tool and forbidden native-helper reasons, not to arbitrary CLI crashes or malformed transport failures.

Claude and Copilot keep usable sessions when a history or pending-tool mismatch cannot safely continue. Corrected history can use the same session. Copilot closes an uncertain effort switch instead of inferring with an unconfirmed setting or replaying it. Claude forced-tool mismatches are final; Gateway does not retry with a smaller catalog. A known pre-inference authentication rejection retains its separate bounded recovery behavior. Claude live sessions must affirm that no native output or tool-result handoff occurred before that retry is admitted. Such a native authentication rejection closes without a crash hold, allowing the next caller request to try again. Failures after output or tool handoff retain the hold; a repaired login does not authorize replaying uncertain work.

Both live CLI routes preserve public reasoning as typed summaries. The live ledger skips those summaries while retaining their rendered positions; converting them into ordinary assistant messages would falsely refuse a valid continuation after tools. A previously preserved Copilot session can accept corrected typed history without a restart, a reseed or another full-history replay.

Live CLI conversations require a stable caller identity. Anonymous first questions remain standalone, while anonymous historical conversations are refused. Gateway never merges chats by prompt similarity or arbitrary user identity. Native Claude Code's validated session metadata and the supported session/thread headers provide that identity across clients.

Genuine model, system/tool catalog and compaction-window changes, completed client compaction, expired/dead sessions and full inference-process restarts can require a new seed. They are not free, and cache reuse is never guaranteed by session presence. The cache safety guard remains a bounded backstop, not an account-wide spending ceiling.

Evidence and operations

The app's Diagnostics screen reports cache samples and reads/writes by model on the inference Mac. gateway diagnostics --since 1 also reports Claude and Copilot session decisions. Blocked and preserved session decisions appear among diagnostic issues. Prompts and tool arguments are not added to logs.

The final ingress audit also covers Claude Desktop's separate auxiliary native classifier. These are independent tool-free classification calls, rather than continued agent chats. They retain their native request controls and use a separate bounded cache budget, including usage reported before a later failure.

Native Copilot 1.0.97 and 1.0.98 were qualified against a loopback synthetic API: three acknowledged immediate messages while a tool waited made no additional inference; delivering its result produced one continuation containing all three messages and the result. Two model calls served the whole loop. This proves protocol ordering, not real subscription pricing parity.

The November 1 audit found prefix caching explicitly disabled on both Qwen workers after an earlier exact tool-input corruption. That is a server correctness limit, not evidence that Gateway discarded a session. An isolated aligned-checkpoint trial has its own dual-router drain, immutable image checks, memory floor and independent recovery. Its outcome must be recorded before enabling that candidate; neither a successful HTTP reply nor stable routing establishes cache correctness.

See Claude sessions, Copilot sessions, Grok limits, and diagnostics.
